rationale: Two independent defects in the pointer/layout kernel, both reached through Pulp's own host-to-view seam. First: hover was the only pointer phase with no portable delivery verb. deliver_mouse_down, deliver_mouse_drag and deliver_mouse_up each fan a native event out to the hover-state pass, the modern on_mouse_event channel and the JS on_dom_pointer_* channel, but a buttonless move had nothing, so every native host open-coded it as a bare View::simulate_hover. simulate_hover raises set_hovered and calls on_hover_move; it runs no JavaScript. A scripted UI therefore saw pointerdown, pointermove-while-dragging and pointerup but never a plain hover, and a handler that picks the cursor from the pointer position only ever ran once a button went down -- the defect a user reports as 'the cursor only changes when I click'. deliver_hover_move adds the missing verb with the same three-step contract the other phases already assert: hover state first so a handler reading is_hovered() during dispatch sees the state this move established; hit-test AFTER that pass, because an on_hover_move handler may restructure the tree and a target captured beforehand could already be detached; then the modern and JS channels with button == MouseButton::none and is_down == false, so no handler mistakes a hover for a held primary button. The ordering hazard is the reason the hit-test moved after the state pass rather than sharing one lookup, and callers must resolve the cursor after this returns, never before, because the value worth publishing is the one the scripted handler just set. Second: yoga_measure echoed the whole AtMost offer back as measured width for a view reporting no intrinsic width. AtMost offers an upper bound, not an assignment -- CSS resolves it to min(max-content, available) -- and a soft-wrapping Label deliberately reports no intrinsic width because its parent decides where lines break. Echoing the offer made every auto-width ANCESTOR of such a label stretch to fill instead of hugging its text. The fix asks the label for its unwrapped max_content_width and clamps to the offer, leaving the widthless-Undefined path (report zero, do not echo NaN) and the constrained Exactly path untouched. Nothing about capture, focus, wheel routing, scroll, or the drag/down/up contracts changed; the comment edits in the header only repoint a stale test filename. This is Pulp-only. Both bugs are artifacts of how Pulp owns the seam between a native host and a scripted view tree: the hover gap exists because Pulp asks each platform host to synthesise pointer delivery itself rather than owning one event pipeline, and the AtMost bug exists because Pulp bridges its own Label measurement into Yoga through a measure callback. A Vellum-native retained UI kernel should own pointer delivery as a single pipeline with no per-host open-coding, and should resolve intrinsic sizing from its own text model rather than through a dynamic_cast in a Yoga measure hook, so neither shape is something Vellum should inherit. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit being backported here, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement.
